fullAnalysis: Puzzle #676 resolves to "Words that come after mega" because every clue becomes a familiar mega compound once you test the prefix instead of chasing a loose science theme.
Megaphone, megahit, megastar, megabyte, and megavolt all work cleanly. Once two of those land, the rest of the board verifies the same mega pattern without exceptions.

wordHints.Phone: Megaphone is the loudest anchor in the set and usually gives the pattern away first.
wordHints.Hit: Megahit is a standard term for a very large commercial success.
wordHints.Star: Megastar fits the same prefix rule in entertainment language.
wordHints.Byte: Megabyte confirms that the pattern also works in computing.
wordHints.Volt: Megavolt closes the loop with a science term that still uses the same mega prefix.

lessons.title: Prefix boards look random until you test one starter word
lessons.body: Phone, hit, and star seem completely unrelated until you try mega in front of each one. When a board mixes entertainment, tech, and science words, a shared prefix is a strong candidate.

lessons.title: Megaphone is the fastest unlock
lessons.body: Megaphone is such a familiar everyday word that it rarely requires a second thought. Once it points you to mega, apply the same prefix to the rest of the board before exploring other options.

lessons.title: Cross-domain prefixes are a classic Pinpoint trick
lessons.body: Mega appears in pop culture (megastar), computing (megabyte), and physics (megavolt). Pinpoint uses cross-domain word families because they are genuinely tricky — the clues feel unrelated until the shared prefix clicks.
